prompt:
Style: neon-thick-impasto. Transform the supplied ORIGINAL photograph of a LEGO Millennium Falcon model on a white cabinet, minifigures, a display plaque and nearby autumn foliage. Render only a single full-frame artwork using this style treatment:

- **Top panel.** The original photograph preserved faithfully, with only subtle exposure, contrast and white-balance correction; nothing stylized, retouched, added, removed, replaced or rearranged. - **Bottom panel — fidelity.** The same crop as the top panel, keeping the same scene, composition, perspective, subject positions, object sizes and spatial relationships. - **Bottom panel — medium.** Repainted as richly textured thick impasto acrylic/oil painting: visible palette-knife marks, broad flat-brush strokes, layered paint ridges, tactile canvas grain and occasional paint drips, with paint blocks appearing to protrude from the canvas. Skies carry swirling, flowing brush marks, buildings become thick blocks of color, and ground reflections read as paint pulled downward with a brush. - **Bottom panel — color.** An expressive, highly saturated neon-leaning palette — magenta, hot pink, orange, electric blue, teal and violet, with restrained yellow highlights — with color placement following the original photograph. Sky, buildings and sea reflections render like neon lights, bright with a slight outward glow, set against deep blue and deep purple shadows so the bright colors stand out, as if the painting were faintly glowing. Softer traditional oil-painting tones are avoided. Readable in-scene signage counts as part of the scene and is preserved. - **Best subjects.** Recommended especially for sunset, night-scene and reflection photos, where the contrast is strongest. 

Preserve the original scene's subject relationships. Every part of the canvas must belong to the transformed artwork. No original photo panel, no before/after comparison, no split, no text.
